newsitem.title: USA: Govt Technology sees increased returns - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Govt Technology sees increased returns - Barron's.

text.p: Government Technology Services Inc new chief Michael Dendy Young believes the profit levels the company earned a few years ago are numbers that shareholders should expect in years to come, Barron's said.
The company earned $1.50 per share in 1991 and $1.30 per share in 1993. Wall Street expects the computer reseller to earn about $0.12 a share this year, and $0.51 in 1997.

But Young, who joined the company after it was put on the sale block in 1995 after a sharp fall in profits, said Government Technology will focus on taking the company to a level "never dreamt of in the past" and that "that kind of return (of the early 90's) is absolutely possible" in the future.
Barron's said that at $6 and change, Government Technology is selling for its net working capital. Book value is almost $9 a share.
It said that while the company is still losing money, it is losing less than it did in the first half last year.
Barron's also said the company makes most of its money in the third and fourth quarters, making first half comparisons less meaningful.
